html:
From 1649 to 1653 the English Parliament's army, led at first by Oliver Cromwell, conquered Ireland, which had been in revolt since 1641.

Cromwell landed in August 1649. At Drogheda and Wexford his troops massacred garrisons and many townspeople, events still bitterly remembered. The war, with famine and plague, killed a large share of Ireland's population; estimates run to a fifth or more.

Afterwards most land owned by Catholics was confiscated and given to soldiers and investors. Catholic landowners were sent west of the Shannon, to Connacht. Catholics had owned most of the land in 1641; by the end of the century they held only a small part. It created the Protestant landed class that ruled Ireland until the Land War and set the stage for the Boyne. It followed the Plantation of Ulster.
sum: From 1649 to 1653 the English Parliament's army, led at first by Oliver Cromwell, conquered Ireland, which had been in revolt since 1641.
